newsitem.title: USA: Pemex negotiating extending Saudi contract - source.
newsitem.headline: Pemex negotiating extending Saudi contract - source.

text.p: Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) is negotiating with Saudi Arabia to extend by two months a contract to import propane from Saudi Arabia, a Pemex source said Friday.

The source, a top trader for the Mexican state-owned oil and gas monopoly, said the additional cargoes will cover Mexico's demand for the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) until its downed Cactus plant returns online in April.
Cactus, the largest gas processing plant in Mexico, has been running at about 50 percent capacity since a July 26, 1996 explosion that knocked out two of its five units.
Pre-explosion output at the plant in southern Mexico was between 50,000 to 70,000 barrels per day (bpd) of LPGs.
In August, Pemex signed a contract with Saudi Arabia to buy one 42,000-tonne (about 520,000 barrels) cargo of propane each month between September and March.
"We are still talking with Saudi Arabia," said the source. "Our last cargo is in February and it will all depend on the pricing if we buy another one."
"My understanding is the Cactus plant will be on in April, so we will have two months to cover," the source, based in Mexico City, added.

The supplier, however, may not necessarily be Saudi Arabia. The source said Pemex officials will be attending the International Petroleum Week conference in London next week and plan to talk with several other suppliers.
